MACRO_SLATE_RECAP.focus: Cross-league trends, regression candidates, aesthetic watchability power rankings.
MACRO_SLATE_RECAP.example_prompt_hook: Analyze the full league slate. Identify macro-level trends across the schedule, diagnose fraudulent records winning ugly on variance, and rank the aesthetic watchability of the week's most electric sandboxes.
MACRO_SLATE_RECAP.directive:
ARTICLE TYPE SPECIFICATION: The Macro Slate Recap
Granularity: Week-level.
Focus: Cross-league trends, regression candidates, aesthetic watchability power rankings.
Scope: You are writing across the entire week's slate. Synthesize high-level patterns across multiple matchups, isolate lucky or unlucky teams using point differentials and tempo, and contextualize what this specific week meant for the broader NFL landscape.
MACRO_SLATE_RECAP.curatorial_autonomy:
CURATORIAL AUTONOMY (MACRO_SLATE_RECAP):
You are provided with the full scoreboard and metrics for the week. Do not write a traditional, chronological recap of a single game. You must select 3 to 4 games that collectively illustrate a larger league-wide trend. Look for a weekend defined by high Upset Leverage ($U$) across multiple favorites, a sudden drop in Offensive Pace ($P$) across the league, or a dominance of high-variance shootouts. Select the games that best serve as evidence for your overarching macro thesis.

PLAYER_DEEP_PROFILE.name: The Player Deep Profile
PLAYER_DEEP_PROFILE.focus: Prestige, longform player profile evaluating their season-to-date trajectory, breakout status, MVP credentials, or legacy implications.
PLAYER_DEEP_PROFILE.curatorial_autonomy:
CURATORIAL AUTONOMY (PLAYER SELECTION):
You are provided with the season-to-date player leaderboards, cumulative stats, and popularity indices. You must select one player whose current campaign defines the narrative of the league. Look for an aging legend desperately trying to preserve their Awards Equity and Playoff Clout, an MVP frontrunner with a massive cultural footprint, or a volatile breakout star who leads the league in explosive ceiling performances. Pick a player whose individual story carries massive historical or cultural weight, regardless of whether it is Week 3 or Week 17.
PLAYER_DEEP_PROFILE.structure_directive:
ARTICLE STRUCTURE & FORMATTING DIRECTIVE:
Structure your article as a prestige, longform player profile summarizing their season-to-date campaign and career trajectory (approx. 800–1,200 words).

1. The Defining Moment (The Hook):
Start with a captivating headline using #.
Write a rich, scene-setting introduction that isolates one defining moment, stretch of games, or overarching narrative from their season so far. Do not list their stat line immediately; focus on the feeling of watching them play this year.

2. The Anatomy of Their Season:
Use a ## header (e.g., ## The Engine of the Offense).
Break down how they produced their numbers. Weave in their Boom-or-Bust Volatility (SpikeIndex) and their overall Offensive Rhythm. Did they carry a bad roster? Did they benefit from an elite supporting cast?

3. The Cultural Footprint & Legacy:
Use a ## header (e.g., ## The Weight of the Crown).
Analyze where this season places them in the historical hierarchy. You must discuss their National Cultural Footprint ($Pop_{\text{player}}$) and the platform their franchise provides. Analyze how this season impacts their Championship Pedigree and Awards Equity.

4. The Horizon:
Use a ### header to look toward the remainder of their career.
End with a poignant thought on what their legacy will be if their trajectory continues, or how quickly their window might close. End sharply. Do not use wrap-up filler.
PLAYER_DEEP_PROFILE.directive:
ARTICLE TYPE SPECIFICATION: The Player Deep Profile
Granularity: In-Season Trajectory / Career Arc.
Focus: Aging superstars, breakthrough rookie sensations, MVP debates, legacy vs. twilight.
Scope: Do not write a generic game recap. Center your entire piece around the emotional, physical, and schematic journey of a singular marquee player across their season-to-date campaign.
PLAYER_DEEP_PROFILE.example_prompt_hook: Select a marquee player whose campaign currently defines the season. Deliver a definitive longform profile on their offensive engine, their cultural footprint, and their career horizon based on their season-to-date tape.

FRANCHISE_STATE_OF_THE_UNION.name: The Franchise State of the Union
FRANCHISE_STATE_OF_THE_UNION.focus: General Manager job security, roster demographic distributions, draft hit rates, rebuilding vs. purgatory.
FRANCHISE_STATE_OF_THE_UNION.example_prompt_hook: Analyze a franchise in transition. Ignore the single-game box score. Evaluate their front office's 3-to-5 year trajectory using the Purgatory Penalty, aging roster constraints, and draft equity.
FRANCHISE_STATE_OF_THE_UNION.directive:
ARTICLE TYPE SPECIFICATION: The Franchise State of the Union
Granularity: 3-to-5 year franchise trajectory.
Focus: General Manager job security, roster demographic distributions, draft hit rates, rebuilding vs. purgatory.
Scope: Step away from the in-game action. Evaluate the organizational health, roster construction cycle, and coaching/front-office stability of a specific franchise through the eyes of rival executives, scouts, and decision-makers.
FRANCHISE_STATE_OF_THE_UNION.curatorial_autonomy:
CURATORIAL AUTONOMY (FRANCHISE_STATE_OF_THE_UNION):
You are provided with full multi-year franchise data, roster demographic distributions, and standing trends. Do not select a stable, well-run contender operating normally within its window. You must identify a franchise sitting at an existential organizational fork in the road:
- An aging roster actively triggering the Purgatory Penalty, stuck hovering around .500 with diminished future assets.
- A high Base Market Gravity ($B$) or storied Legacy Floor ($S_{\text{all-time}}$) franchise collapsing under market pressure and fan expectations.
- A rebuilding organization with immense Blue-Chip Pedigree ($P_{\text{draft}}$) and elite Under-25 Production Share ($Y_{\text{prod}}$) on the precipice of entering a multi-year contention window.
Select the single organization whose front office, coaching hierarchy, or foundational blueprint demands a comprehensive, multi-year audit.

COACHING DATA: Call `get_coach_profile` to judge the coaching hierarchy: tenure, who he replaced, record with the team, career playoff record, schemes and tendencies. Tendencies are Low / Medium / High staff tendencies: describe them, never turn them into percentages or per-game counts.

SINGLE_GAME_SCHEMATIC_AUTOPSY.name: The Single-Game Schematic Autopsy
SINGLE_GAME_SCHEMATIC_AUTOPSY.focus: Point-of-attack wins, run-pass splits, specific receiver coverage isolations, quarterback processing mechanics, and the defensive playmakers who swung the game.
data_queried: Advanced Game Analytics (Offensive Pace, Single-Game Excitement)
Game defensive lines (tackles, sacks, TFL, INT, pass deflections, forced fumbles) and kickers, where captured
SINGLE_GAME_SCHEMATIC_AUTOPSY.example_prompt_hook: Select a single compelling matchup from the slate. Break down the play-level tactical mechanics that decided the outcome: offensive pace, point-of-attack leverage, and individual matchup exploitation.
SINGLE_GAME_SCHEMATIC_AUTOPSY.directive:
ARTICLE TYPE SPECIFICATION: The Single-Game Schematic Autopsy
Granularity: Single-game play-by-play.
Focus: Point-of-attack wins, run-pass splits, specific receiver coverage isolations, quarterback processing mechanics, and the defensive playmakers who swung the game.
Scope: Focus laser-sharp on one specific game's tactical blueprint. Chart why the game unfolded the way it did using evidence-based film charting principles, tactical concepts, and efficiency data rather than narrative or emotion.
SINGLE_GAME_SCHEMATIC_AUTOPSY.curatorial_autonomy:
CURATORIAL AUTONOMY (SINGLE_GAME_SCHEMATIC_AUTOPSY):
You are given the full league slate. Ignore narratives, market size, and playoff implications. You must select the single game with the most extreme tactical anomaly. Look for an abnormally high Offensive Pace ($P$), a massive SpikeIndex from a heavily schemed player, or a game where the Opponent-Adjusted Game Credit exposes a glaring mismatch. Choose the game that offers the best "film room" educational value regarding blocking concepts, coverage shells, or specific play-calling.
A game decided by defense qualifies too (a pass rush that lived in the backfield, a secondary that took the ball away, a defensive score), but only if `get_game_box_score` returns defensive lines for it. Describe scheme as your read of the box score; never cite pressure rates, blitz rates, coverage percentages, snap counts or targets, which aren't recorded. When the box score has `team_situational` lines (third-down conversions, red-zone trips, quarter-by-quarter scoring, time of possession), use them for the game's situational story; when it doesn't, compare the teams' season rates from `get_team_efficiency_profile` and don't invent the game's third-down or red-zone numbers.

COACHING DATA: For the schematic story, call `get_matchup_edges` with the game's two teams and read its `coaching_matchup` block (each offense's scheme, pass lean and fourth-down tendency against the other defense's front and coverage tendency), or `get_coach_profile` for either staff. Tendencies are Low / Medium / High staff tendencies: describe them, never turn them into percentages or per-game counts.

POWER_RANKINGS.name: The Power Rankings (32-Team Thematic Consensus)
POWER_RANKINGS.focus: Comprehensive publication-ready 32-team Power Ranking evaluating every team 1-32 through an explicit weekly editorial theme, underlying metrics, and movement indicators.
POWER_RANKINGS.curatorial_autonomy:
CURATORIAL AUTONOMY (32-TEAM POWER RANKINGS SELECTION):
You are provided with full standings, game outcomes, and advanced analytics for all 32 teams. Do not simply copy the raw win-loss standings. Evaluate the true hierarchy across the league by cross-referencing on-field success with underlying metrics:
- Separate true contenders from "paper tigers" carrying inflated records against soft schedules using Opponent-Adjusted Game Credit.
- Reward teams surging on positive underlying efficiency via the Trajectory Multiplier ($T$).
- Penalize aging, stagnating squads sliding into middle-tier mediocrity under the Purgatory Penalty.
You must establish an explicit Weekly Editorial Theme across the piece (e.g., "First-Month Verdicts", "The Four-Word Season Diagnosis", or "Fatal Flaws and Championship Ceilings"). Every individual team entry must directly answer this unifying theme rather than offering a generic game recap.
POWER_RANKINGS.structure_directive:
ARTICLE STRUCTURE & FORMATTING DIRECTIVE:
Structure your article as a comprehensive, publication-ready 32-team Power Ranking (approx. 1,800–2,400 words).

1. The Macro Overview (The Hook):
Open with a journalistic headline using # (e.g., # NFL Power Rankings Week 5: 1-32 Hierarchy and First-Month Realities).
Write a 2-paragraph introduction outlining the battle for the #1 spot and the overarching narrative defining the league this week.
Explicitly define the Weekly Theme that governs the evaluations for all 32 franchises.

2. The 32-Team Enumeration (Strict Rule):
You must rank and write an entry for EVERY SINGLE TEAM FROM 1 TO 32 without exception. Do not truncate the list, do not summarize teams in groups, and do not stop after the top 10.
Use numbered ## headers formatted exactly as: ## [Rank]. [City] [Team] ([W-L]) (Previous: N | Change: ±N) (e.g., ## 1. Carolina Panthers (4-0) (Previous: 3 | Change: +2)).
Take the previous ranks from the POWER RANKINGS CONTINUITY section; use "--" for no change, and "(Previous: — | New)" when no earlier ranking exists.

3. The Thematic Blurb Requirements:
Begin each team blurb with a bold thematic kicker matching the intro hook (e.g., Four-word recap: Living on borrowed time. or First-month verdict: Elite defense masking passing stalls.).
Follow immediately with exactly 3 to 4 analytical sentences evaluating the franchise.
Data Integration Rule: Translate underlying database metrics into natural football terminology. Cite tempo and per-possession scoring pace, draft pedigree, youth production share, or opponent-adjusted quality without displaying raw mathematical symbols (avoid $P$, $T$, $W$, P_draft, etc.).

4. The Walk-Off (The Drop-Off):
After completing team # 32, conclude with a single concise paragraph evaluating the widening gap between the league's inner-circle contenders and the bottom tier.
Do not use formulaic sign-offs like "In conclusion" or "To summarize." End cleanly once the final thought is stated.
POWER_RANKINGS.directive:
ARTICLE TYPE SPECIFICATION: The Power Rankings (32-Team Thematic Consensus)
Granularity: Week-level / Full League 1-32 Hierarchy.
Focus: Comprehensive, publication-ready 32-team Power Ranking evaluating every team 1-32 through an explicit weekly editorial theme, underlying metrics, and movement indicators.
Scope: Rank and write an entry for all 32 NFL franchises from 1 to 32. Establish a unifying weekly editorial theme, evaluate paper tigers vs. true contenders, and provide tight thematic blurbs for every team.
POWER_RANKINGS.example_prompt_hook: Rank all 32 NFL franchises from 1 to 32 under an explicit weekly editorial theme. Separate paper tigers from true contenders using opponent-adjusted credit and trajectory, provide a 3-to-4 sentence analytical blurb for every team with movement indicators, and diagnose the widening gap between tiers.

AWARDS_TRACKER.name: The Awards Tracker
AWARDS_TRACKER.focus: Active MVP, OPOY, OROY, DPOY, DROY and Coach of the Year races, evaluating true contenders vs. empty-calorie stat accumulators, narrative momentum, rookie learning curves, the defenders driving the defensive races, and which head coaches are winning more than their rosters should.
data_queried: Defense season leaders (sacks, TFL, interceptions, takeaways; rookies flagged)
Coach of the Year race (COTY score, wins above expectation, roster outperformance, improvement over last season)
AWARDS_TRACKER.curatorial_autonomy:
CURATORIAL AUTONOMY (AWARDS WATCH SELECTION):
You are provided with the cumulative season stats, team records, and popularity indices. You must evaluate the active race for MVP, Offensive Player of the Year, Offensive Rookie of the Year, Defensive Player of the Year, and Defensive Rookie of the Year, plus the Coach of the Year race. You must aggressively apply the "Empty Calories" Suppressor—ignore players racking up meaningless stats on sub-.300 teams. You are looking for the rare intersection of elite, highly-visible statistical production (SpikeIndex) and the narrative weight of playing on a true contender ($T_{\text{success}}$). For Coach of the Year, start from get_coach_of_the_year_race: credit the coach whose team is winning more than its roster, its schedule-adjusted strength and last season say it should, not simply the best record.

DEFENSIVE AWARDS EVIDENCE:
- Build the Defensive Player of the Year race from `get_defense_special_teams_leaders` (sacks, tackles_for_loss, interceptions and takeaways first; forced_fumbles, pass_deflections and defensive_tds as tiebreakers) and confirm each candidate with `get_player_season_stats`.
- Build the Defensive Rookie of the Year race the same way with `rookies_only=True`. A rookie is a player in his first season (years of experience 0).
- Every defensive candidate's case rests on recorded numbers. Madden lists only its statistical leaders (defenders by tackles), so a defender with no recorded line has unknown numbers, not zeros: don't name him as a candidate and never invent his stats. Never cite pressures, snap counts or coverage numbers, which aren't recorded.
- Team record matters less for the defensive awards than for MVP, but a dominant season on a winning team still beats the same numbers on a losing one.
AWARDS_TRACKER.structure_directive:
ARTICLE STRUCTURE & FORMATTING DIRECTIVE:
Structure your article as an elite "Awards Watch" column (approx. 1,100–1,400 words).

1. The MVP Frontrunner (The Heavy Crown):
Start with a definitive headline using #.
Use a ## header to identify the clear MVP favorite. Analyze how their National Cultural Footprint ($Pop_{\text{player}}$) and their team's record are shaping the media narrative in their favor. Detail how they are carrying their offense.

2. The Contenders (The Chasers):
Use a ## header to list 2-3 players within striking distance of the frontrunner.
Compare their Boom-or-Bust Volatility (SpikeIndex) against the favorite. If a contender has massive Historical Franchise Prestige on their side, explain how that narrative momentum could help them steal the award late in the year.

3. The Coach of the Year Race:
Use a ## header for the Coach of the Year race. Name the frontrunner and one or two challengers from get_coach_of_the_year_race, and make each case with the team's record, wins above expectation, how far they are outperforming their roster's rating, and the jump from last season where it is recorded.

4. The Offensive Rookie Race:
Use a ## header devoted entirely to the Offensive Rookie of the Year race. Focus on rookie performance considering the learning curve of the NFL.
Highlight the two or three rookies leading the race.

5. The Defensive Races:
Use a ## header for the Defensive Player of the Year frontrunner and one or two chasers, each backed by his season line (sacks, tackles for loss, interceptions, takeaways). Then use a ### header for the Defensive Rookie of the Year race with the two or three leading rookies and their numbers. End the article sharply after the defensive rookie breakdown.
AWARDS_TRACKER.directive:
ARTICLE TYPE SPECIFICATION: The Awards Tracker
Granularity: Season-level / Hardware Campaign.
Focus: MVP, OPOY, OROY, DPOY, DROY and Coach of the Year hardware races, narrative momentum, and true contenders vs. empty calories.
Scope: Track and debate the active award races across the league. Filter out stat-padders on losing squads and evaluate the intersection of individual brilliance, cultural footprint, and team success.
AWARDS_TRACKER.example_prompt_hook: Analyze the active MVP, OPOY, OROY, DPOY and DROY races across the league. Apply the empty-calories suppressor to eliminate meaningless stats, examine the frontrunner vs. the chasers, rank the Coach of the Year race, break down the offensive rookie race, and settle the defensive races on recorded sacks, tackles for loss and takeaways.

SLATE_LOOKAHEAD_PREDICTIONS.name: The Weekly Slate Lookahead (ESPN Multi-Angle Matchup Preview)
SLATE_LOOKAHEAD_PREDICTIONS.focus: Comprehensive, modular weekly preview guide modeled after ESPN's multi-perspective game capsules covering team context, key stats, watchability, tactical predictions, fantasy spotlights, and projected final scores.
SLATE_LOOKAHEAD_PREDICTIONS.curatorial_autonomy:
CURATORIAL AUTONOMY (SLATE LOOKAHEAD SELECTION):
You are provided with the full upcoming schedule, team records, and advanced team metrics. You must evaluate the entire weekly slate. Do not treat every game identically; curate your analysis through distinct analytical perspectives:
- Identify the high-tempo clashes featuring elite Offensive Pace ($P$) or high Watchability ($W$) to spotlight why fans must tune in.
- Use Upset Leverage ($U$) and underlying regression metrics to flag prime candidates for a shocker where a heavy favorite is vulnerable.
- Analyze specific skill-player mismatches and SpikeIndex volatility to isolate individual breakout opportunities.
You must preview the full slate using an integrated, multi-analyst format covering locker room buzz, analytics, viewing appeal, and fantasy angles.

COACHING DATA: The `coaching_matchup` block of `get_matchup_edges` shows each offense's scheme and tendencies against the opposing defense's front and coverage tendency; use it where a clash of staffs sharpens a pick. Tendencies are Low / Medium / High staff tendencies: describe them, never turn them into percentages or per-game counts.
SLATE_LOOKAHEAD_PREDICTIONS.structure_directive:
ARTICLE STRUCTURE & FORMATTING DIRECTIVE:
Structure your article as a comprehensive, modular weekly preview guide modeled after ESPN's multi-perspective game capsules (approx. 2,000–2,500 words).

1. The Slate Overview (The Hook):
Open with an editorial headline using # (e.g., # NFL Week Lookahead: Matchup Previews, Predictions, Fantasy Angles, and Film Room Notes).
Write a 2-paragraph introduction identifying the defining storylines, high-stakes divisional showdowns, and trap games that shape this slate.
Include a complete matchup jump list detailing every game (e.g., PHI-JAX | CHI-GB | LV-NE | DEN-LAC...).

2. The Full Slate Enumeration (Strict Rule):
You must generate a full preview capsule for EVERY SINGLE GAME on the weekly schedule. Do not omit any matchups. Do not group games together. Do not truncate the list or stop after the marquee games.

3. Modular Matchup Capsules (Strict Structure):
For each game on the schedule, use a ## heading formatted as:
## [Away Team] ([Record]) at [Home Team] ([Record])
Immediately below, add a line with kickoff time and broadcast network (e.g., 1:00 p.m. ET | CBS). Do not include any betting lines.
Inside each matchup capsule, provide the following structured sub-sections:
- What We're Hearing (Team Context): 1–2 short paragraphs detailing locker room sentiment, roster changes, or how the teams are managing pressure. Quote an internal player or coach perspective where fitting.
- Stat to Know: A single high-impact data point contextualizing the matchup (e.g., defensive split vs. explosive passing, a third-down or red-zone rate and its league rank from `get_team_efficiency_profile`, or per-possession tempo).
- Why You Should Watch This Game: 1–2 sharp, engaging sentences highlighting the game's aesthetic appeal, schematic drama, or player matchup that makes it appointment viewing.
- Bold Prediction & Tactical Angle: A data-driven forecast explaining how a schematic advantage (e.g., point-of-attack blocking or pass rush mismatch) will break the game open.
- Fantasy & Player Spike Spotlight: A targeted analysis of a skill player whose usage or volatility suggests an explosive ceiling or a brutal matchup floor.
- Official Prediction: A concise breakdown of how the game script will unfold, followed by an official projected scoreline:
Projected Final: [Winner] [Score], [Loser] [Score]

4. Data Integration Rule:
Translate all internal analytical engine variables ($P$, $U$, $W$, SpikeIndex, $P_{\text{draft}}$) into authentic football terminology (tempo, high-leverage variance, must-see rating, boom-or-bust ceiling, blue-chip capital). Never output raw variable symbols or formula notation in the published copy.
SLATE_LOOKAHEAD_PREDICTIONS.directive:
ARTICLE TYPE SPECIFICATION: The Weekly Slate Lookahead (ESPN Multi-Angle Matchup Preview)
Granularity: Week-ahead / Matchup Preview Guide.
Focus: Comprehensive, modular weekly preview guide modeled after ESPN's multi-perspective game capsules covering team context, key stats, watchability, tactical predictions, fantasy spotlights, and projected final scores.
Scope: Deliver in-depth, structured game capsules for featured matchups across the slate. Combine locker-room context, key metrics, viewer appeal, fantasy outlook, and final score projections without displaying raw algebraic variables.
SLATE_LOOKAHEAD_PREDICTIONS.example_prompt_hook: Preview the upcoming weekend slate using ESPN-style modular game capsules. For each featured matchup, break down locker-room buzz, a key statistical split, why fans should tune in, a bold tactical forecast, fantasy spike spotlight, and an official final score prediction.

PLAYOFF_PREDICTOR.name: The Playoff Predictor
PLAYOFF_PREDICTOR.focus: Projected postseason bracket mapping, identifying fraudulent division leaders ripe for first-round upsets, and dangerous Wild Card gatecrashers.
PLAYOFF_PREDICTOR.curatorial_autonomy:
CURATORIAL AUTONOMY (PLAYOFF PREDICTION SELECTION):
You are provided with the current standings, wild-card tiebreakers, and team metrics. You must map out the projected postseason bracket. Do not simply chalk the current #1 seeds into the Super Bowl. You must identify the "fraudulent" division leaders who are ripe for a first-round upset due to poor Opponent-Adjusted Game Credit, and identify the terrifying Wild Card teams surging on a massive Trajectory spike. Frame your selections around which teams present the most dangerous matchup nightmare in a single-elimination setting.
PLAYOFF_PREDICTOR.structure_directive:
ARTICLE STRUCTURE & FORMATTING DIRECTIVE:
Structure your article as a definitive "Playoff Picture & Predictions" column (approx. 800–1,000 words).

1. The Postseason Landscape (The Hook):
Start with a definitive headline using #.
Write a 2-paragraph introduction defining the current shape of the conferences. Is it a top-heavy year dominated by two juggernauts, or a chaotic, wide-open race?

2. The Bracket Locks (The Favorites):
Use a ## header (e.g., ## The Divisional Round By-passers).
Identify the 2-3 teams that are mathematically and structurally built to make deep runs. Weave in their Offensive Rhythm and Baseline Roster Talent to explain why they are immune to early-round upsets.

3. The Dangerous Gatecrashers (The Wild Cards):
Use a ## header to highlight 1-2 lower-seeded teams no one wants to face in January.
Highlight their Boom-or-Bust Volatility or their explosive Youth Production Share. Explain exactly how their high-variance style can ruin a #2 seed's season on Wild Card weekend.

4. The First-Round Exit Warning:
Use a ### header to place one current playoff team on "Upset Alert."
Detail why their underlying metrics (like a low offensive tempo or reliance on lucky turnover margins) guarantee they will be eliminated in the first round. Stop immediately after delivering the warning.
PLAYOFF_PREDICTOR.directive:
ARTICLE TYPE SPECIFICATION: The Playoff Predictor
Granularity: Late-Season / Playoff Race.
Focus: Postseason bracketology, true contenders vs. fraudulent division winners, and dangerous Wild Card spoilers.
Scope: Project the postseason bracket and pathing. Interrogate top seeds for first-round vulnerability and isolate surging lower seeds with matchup nightmare profiles.
PLAYOFF_PREDICTOR.example_prompt_hook: Map out the projected postseason bracket. Expose a fraudulent division leader on upset alert, identify the terrifying Wild Card gatecrashers, and establish the true conference heavyweights.

SUPER_BOWL_CONTENDER_BLUEPRINT.name: The Super Bowl Contender Blueprint
SUPER_BOWL_CONTENDER_BLUEPRINT.focus: Championship contender autopsy evaluating whether top-tier teams possess the statistical profile, quarterback clout, and roster balance to win three straight playoff games.
SUPER_BOWL_CONTENDER_BLUEPRINT.curatorial_autonomy:
CURATORIAL AUTONOMY (SUPER BOWL CONTENDER SELECTION):
You are provided with the elite top-tier teams in the NFL. Your job is to separate the "very good regular season teams" from the "actual Super Bowl champions." Evaluate the league's heavyweights strictly through the lens of championship criteria. Look for the exact statistical profile required to win a ring: elite quarterback Awards Equity, battle-tested veteran Playoff Clout, and a balanced Youth Production Share. You must aggressively dismiss pretenders who lack the schematic balance or the historical pedigree to win three straight games against elite competition.
SUPER_BOWL_CONTENDER_BLUEPRINT.structure_directive:
ARTICLE STRUCTURE & FORMATTING DIRECTIVE:
Structure your article as a rigid "Championship Contender Autopsy" (approx. 1,000 words).

1. The Championship Standard (The Hook):
Start with a definitive headline using #.
Write a 1-2 paragraph introduction outlining exactly what traits are required to win the Lombardi Trophy this season. Establish the barrier to entry (e.g., "If you don't have an elite Offensive Tempo, you cannot win in January").

2. The Blue-Chip Heavyweights (The Inner Circle):
Use ## headers to break down the 2-3 teams that check every championship box.
You must weave in their veteran Championship Pedigree, their Historical Franchise Prestige, and the overwhelming Baseline Roster Talent that makes them the definitive favorites.

3. The Paper Tigers (The Fatal Flaw):
Use a ## header (e.g., ## The Pretenders).
Identify a team with 11+ wins that cannot win the Super Bowl. You must diagnose their fatal flaw using natural language metrics—whether it is a lack of Playoff Clout under center, a red-zone touchdown rate or third-down rate that ranks near the bottom of the league (`get_team_efficiency_profile`), or an aging roster suffering from the Purgatory Penalty masquerading as a contender.

4. The Missing Piece:
Use a ### header to identify one elite team that is exactly one piece away.
Briefly state what they need (e.g., a secondary playmaker or an edge rusher) to elevate from a playoff team to a Super Bowl champion. End the column sharply.
SUPER_BOWL_CONTENDER_BLUEPRINT.directive:
ARTICLE TYPE SPECIFICATION: The Super Bowl Contender Blueprint
Granularity: Championship / Postseason Arc.
Focus: Championship DNA, true Lombardi contenders vs. regular-season pretenders, and missing pieces.
Scope: Apply a rigid championship litmus test to the league's top teams. Separate 11-win paper tigers from battle-tested heavyweights equipped to win the Lombardi Trophy.
SUPER_BOWL_CONTENDER_BLUEPRINT.example_prompt_hook: Apply the championship litmus test to the league's top tier. Crown the inner-circle heavyweights, dissect an 11-win paper tiger with a fatal playoff flaw, and identify the contender that is one piece away.

LOCAL_POSTGAME_REPORT_CARD.name: The Postgame Report Card (The Beat Gradeout)
LOCAL_POSTGAME_REPORT_CARD.focus: Immediate unit execution versus expectations, unit letter grades (A+ through F), offensive line protection breakdowns, third-down stalls, and coaching decisions.
LOCAL_POSTGAME_REPORT_CARD.curatorial_autonomy:
CURATORIAL AUTONOMY (LOCAL POSTGAME FOCUS):
You are covering strictly this franchise. Do not compare this game to the broader national slate. Your filter is immediate execution versus expectations. You are isolating which specific positional unit won or lost this game. Prioritize third-down conversion failures, offensive line protection breakdowns, and sudden schematic collapses over broad narrative platitudes. Cite the game's third-down, red-zone and penalty numbers only from the box score's `team_situational` line; when the game has none, judge the unit against its season rates from `get_team_efficiency_profile` and don't invent the game's totals.

COACHING DATA: Grade coaching decisions against the staff's known tendencies from `get_coach_profile` (an aggressive fourth-down coach who kicked, a run-heavy offense that abandoned the run) using what the box score records. Tendencies are Low / Medium / High staff tendencies: describe them, never turn them into percentages or per-game counts.
LOCAL_POSTGAME_REPORT_CARD.structure_directive:
ARTICLE STRUCTURE & FORMATTING DIRECTIVE:
Structure your article as an immediate, granular postgame assessment (approx. 700–900 words).

1. The Instant Takeaway:
- Open with a direct headline using # focused on the central reason for the outcome (e.g., # Report Card: Protection Breakdowns Sink Second-Half Surge).
- Deliver a 2-paragraph summary of the game's turning point and the overall performance grade.

2. The Unit-by-Unit Grades:
- Use ## headers to evaluate every core unit:
  * ## Passing Offense
  * ## Rushing Attack
  * ## Front Seven & Run Defense
  * ## Secondary & Pass Rush
  * ## Special Teams & Coaching Decisions

Structure your article as a prestige Top 10 positional countdown (approx. 1,000–1,200 words).

Write a 1-paragraph introduction establishing the criteria for this specific Top 10. Explain what separates the #1 overall player from the rest of the top 5.

2. The Top 10 Countdown:
Use numbered ## headers for every player (e.g., ## 1. [Player Name], [Team]).

PLAYOFF_AUTOPSY.directive:
ARTICLE TYPE SPECIFICATION: The Playoff Autopsy
Granularity: Postseason Exit / Offseason Horizon.
Focus: Forensic examination of an eliminated playoff team, schematic breakdown of their postseason exit, championship window trajectory, and offseason front-office mandate.
Scope: Deliver a definitive postseason autopsy on a newly eliminated franchise. Diagnose the tactical malfunction that doomed their playoff run, evaluate the age curve of their core, and set the terms of their upcoming offseason without speculating on specific salary figures or trade proposals.
PLAYOFF_AUTOPSY.curatorial_autonomy:
CURATORIAL AUTONOMY (PLAYOFF_AUTOPSY):
You are provided with the results of the most recent playoff round along with full-season and multi-year franchise analytics. You must select an eliminated team whose exit represents a significant organizational crossroads:
- An aging heavyweight whose championship window appears to have slammed shut under the weight of veteran attrition and the Purgatory Penalty.
- A high Base Market Gravity ($B$) franchise facing immense fan and executive scrutiny after a high-profile collapse or premature exit.
- An ascending young roster powered by elite Under-25 Production Share ($Y_{\text{prod}}$) whose postseason loss served as a foundational learning experience rather than a systemic failure.
Select the eliminated franchise whose exit raises the most urgent structural questions heading into the spring.

COACHING DATA: For the coaching seat-temperature section, call `get_coach_profile` for the eliminated team: the coach's tenure, record with the team, career playoff and Super Bowl record and his schemes and tendencies ground the verdict on whether the staff survives. Tendencies are Low / Medium / High staff tendencies: describe them, never turn them into percentages or per-game counts.
PLAYOFF_AUTOPSY.structure_directive:
ARTICLE STRUCTURE & FORMATTING DIRECTIVE:
Structure your article as a rigorous postseason autopsy and franchise diagnosis (approx. 900–1,200 words).

1. The Scene of the Crash (The Exit):
Open with an authoritative headline using # (e.g., # Playoff Autopsy: How [Opponent] Solved [Team Name] and What Comes Next).
Write 2 paragraphs analyzing the finality of the elimination game. Identify the exact moment or systemic matchup disadvantage that doomed their postseason run.

2. The Schematic Fracture (What Broke on Film):
Use a ## header (e.g., ## The Film Room: Where the Game Plan Fractured).
Break down the specific tactical collapse that decided their fate (e.g., protection breakdown against blitz packages, inability to generate explosive plays against split-safety looks, or red-zone execution failures). Ground situational claims in the elimination game's `team_situational` box-score line and the regular-season rates from `get_team_efficiency_profile`. Contrast their regular-season baseline against this postseason exposure without using raw algebraic variables.

3. The Window Audit (Ascending, Stagnant, or Slamming Shut):
Use a ## header (e.g., ## The Championship Window Litmus Test).
Evaluate the structural age and foundation of the roster. Examine whether the team's core is sustained by high Under-25 Production ($Y_{\text{prod}}$) and incoming draft capital ($P_{\text{draft}}$), or whether the roster is sliding into middle-tier mediocrity under the Purgatory Penalty.

4. Front Office & Coaching Seat Temperature:
Use a ## header (e.g., ## Organizational Heat & Accountability).
Assess the pressure on the coaching staff and front office. Frame whether this playoff defeat demands a schematic overhaul, play-calling adjustments, or patience with an ascending foundation.

5. The Spring Mandate:
Conclude with a ### header stating the singular priority for the upcoming offseason.
Define the specific positional archetype, schematic adjustment, or draft focus required to return to the postseason and advance further next January. Conclude cleanly without transitional wrap-ups.

X_FACTOR_VOLATILITY_SPOTLIGHT.curatorial_autonomy:
CURATORIAL AUTONOMY (X_FACTOR_SPOTLIGHT):
You are provided with the Super Bowl matchup and full-season advanced metrics for both rosters. You must select the ultimate 'X-Factor' player for this specific matchup. Do not pick the star Quarterback, and do not pick a steady, low-variance possession receiver. You are hunting for volatility:
- A boom-or-bust deep threat with a massive SpikeIndex who faces a vulnerable defensive secondary.
- A pass rusher or ball hawk whose sack, tackle-for-loss, interception or forced-fumble totals make a game-wrecking play likely (find them with `get_defense_special_teams_leaders`).
- A returner or kicker who can flip the field or the score.
- A dynamic rookie ($Y_{\text{prod}}$) whose usage has spiked in the postseason, making them an unpredictable variable for the opposing defensive coordinator.
Confirm any candidate's line with `get_player_season_stats`. Madden lists only its leaders, so a defender with no line has unknown numbers, not zeros; never add listed defenders up into team totals; pressures, snap counts and targets aren't recorded, so never cite them.
Select the player whose variance will dictate the final outcome of the game.
X_FACTOR_VOLATILITY_SPOTLIGHT.structure_directive:
ARTICLE STRUCTURE & FORMATTING DIRECTIVE:
Structure your article as a predictive X-Factor breakdown (approx. 800–1,000 words).

1. The Game-Breaker Thesis (The Hook):
Open with a sharp, definitive headline using # (e.g., # The Ultimate X-Factor: Why [Player Name] Holds the Keys to the Super Bowl).
Write a 2-paragraph introduction identifying the player and explaining why the general public is underestimating their potential impact on the game script.

2. The Anatomy of the Spike (The Volatility Audit):
Use a ## header (e.g., ## The Boom-or-Bust Profile).
Translate their SpikeIndex into natural football terminology. Explain their floor vs. their ceiling. When this player hits their absolute peak, what does it look like on the field? Back this up with their recorded numbers: catches, yards, touchdowns and share of the team's touches for a skill player; sacks, tackles for loss, interceptions and forced fumbles for a defender; return yards and touchdowns or long field goals for a specialist. Targets, routes and snap counts aren't recorded.

3. The Schematic Mismatch (The Film Room):
Use a ## header (e.g., ## Exploiting the Matchup).
Break down the specific weakness in the opponent's defense that this player is uniquely equipped to exploit. Detail the tactical alignment (e.g., motioning into the slot against a slower linebacker, or winning one-on-ones on the boundary; for a defender, the protection or quarterback he can punish, using the quarterback's sacks taken and interceptions).

4. The Script Prediction:
Conclude with a ### header projecting their exact Super Bowl output.
Predict whether they will hit their massive ceiling and win the game for their team, or hit their floor and stall the offense. State exactly how many explosive plays (20+ yards) or high-leverage stops they will generate. End cleanly without summary filler.

OFFICIAL_AP_ALL_PRO_ROSTER.directive:
ARTICLE TYPE SPECIFICATION: The Official AP All-Pro Roster
Granularity: Season-Level / Year-End Roster.
Focus: The definitive First and Second-Team AP All-Pro selections, statistical justifications, positional dominance, and voting anomalies.
Scope: Serve as the authoritative publication of record revealing both the First and Second AP All-Pro teams in full. Deliver exhaustive, official roster lists across offense, defense, and special teams with targeted statistical rationale.
OFFICIAL_AP_ALL_PRO_ROSTER.curatorial_autonomy:
CURATORIAL AUTONOMY (ALL-PRO ROSTER SELECTION):
You are selecting and revealing the definitive year-end AP All-Pro roster. You must construct both the complete First Team and Second Team. Weigh full-season efficiency, raw volume, and high-leverage execution. Apply the 'Empty Calories' suppressor aggressively—do not award honors to players racking up garbage-time stats on sub-.300 teams.
- If Field Yates: Focus on the raw statistical dominance and milestone volume (yards and touchdowns, sacks, interceptions, field goals) that separated the First Team from the Second Team.
- If Bill Barnwell: Focus on underlying down-to-down efficiency, positional value, and which defensive totals overstate or understate a player's impact (a linebacker's tackles piling up behind a leaky front, an edge rusher whose tackles for loss say more than his sacks).

DEFENSE & SPECIAL TEAMS EVIDENCE:
- Build the defensive and special-teams ballots from `get_defense_special_teams_leaders`: sacks and tackles_for_loss for edge rushers and interior linemen; tackles, tackles_for_loss and takeaways for linebackers; interceptions, pass_deflections and takeaways for cornerbacks and safeties; field_goals, punting, kick_returns and punt_returns for the specialists. Confirm finalists with `get_player_season_stats`, and check `get_top_rated_players` so no elite defender is missed.
- Madden lists only its statistical leaders (defenders by tackles), so a defender with no line has unknown numbers, not zeros. You may still select him on talent and role, but don't give him a stat line.
- Offensive linemen have only sacks allowed; the fullback, special teamer and long snapper have no meaningful stats. Pick them on talent, role and team results and justify them without numbers.
OFFICIAL_AP_ALL_PRO_ROSTER.structure_directive:
ARTICLE STRUCTURE & FORMATTING DIRECTIVE:
Structure your article as the definitive, publication-ready All-Pro Roster Reveal (approx. 1,400–1,800 words).

1. The Voting Overview (The Hook):
- Open with a definitive headline using # (e.g., # The [Season] AP All-Pro Team: The Official First and Second-Team Rosters).
- Write a 2-paragraph introduction identifying the defining characteristic of this year's voting class (e.g., unanimous selections, a historic rookie class, or a changing of the guard at quarterback).

2. The First-Team Offense:
- Use a ## header (e.g., ## First-Team Offense).
- Output a cleanly formatted Markdown list containing the exact modern AP Offensive slots: 1 QB, 1 RB, 1 FB, 3 WRs, 1 TE, 1 All-Purpose Player, 1 LT, 1 LG, 1 C, 1 RG, 1 RT.
- Provide a brief 1-sentence statistical justification for the skill-position players (QB, RB, WRs, TE) translating their Boom-or-Bust Volatility (SpikeIndex) or Awards Equity into natural football language. Linemen may carry their sacks-allowed figure if they have one.

3. The First-Team Defense & Special Teams:
- Use a ## header (e.g., ## First-Team Defense & Special Teams).
- Output a formatted Markdown list containing the exact modern AP Defensive slots: 2 Edge Rushers, 2 Interior Linemen, 3 Linebackers, 2 Cornerbacks, 1 Slot Cornerback, 2 Safeties.
- Below defense, list the Special Teams slots: 1 Kicker, 1 Punter, 1 Kick Returner, 1 Punt Returner, 1 Special Teamer, 1 Long Snapper.
- Give each First-Team defender and specialist with a recorded line a 1-sentence statistical justification from their season numbers (e.g., sacks and tackles for loss for an edge rusher, interceptions and pass deflections for a cornerback, field goals and 50-plus makes for the kicker, net average for the punter). The special teamer and long snapper get a short role note with no numbers.

4. The Second-Team Offense:
- Use a ## header (e.g., ## Second-Team Offense).
- Output a cleanly formatted Markdown list of the offensive runners-up matching the exact positional slots above.

5. The Second-Team Defense & Special Teams:
- Use a ## header (e.g., ## Second-Team Defense & Special Teams).
- Output a cleanly formatted Markdown list of the defensive and special teams runners-up matching the exact positional slots above.
- End the article cleanly after the Long Snapper. Do not include a concluding summary paragraph.

SUPER_BOWL_COMPREHENSIVE_PREVIEW.curatorial_autonomy:

SUPER_BOWL_COMPREHENSIVE_PREVIEW.structure_directive:
ARTICLE STRUCTURE & FORMATTING DIRECTIVE:
Structure your piece as the premier championship mega-preview (approx. 1,800–2,200 words).

1. The Grand Stage (The Overture):
Open with an authoritative headline using # (e.g., # Super Bowl LXI Preview: Tactical Mismatches, Legacy Stakes, and the Path to the Lombardi Trophy).

Use a ## header (e.g., ## The Schematic Fault Lines: Two-High Shells vs. Motion Concepts).

Use a ## header isolating special teams, turnover margins, and skill-player boom-or-bust variance (SpikeIndex).
Highlight the non-QB unit or situational dynamic (third-down conversions, red-zone touchdowns vs. field goals, penalties) that could suddenly swing momentum, using both teams' season rates and ranks from `get_team_efficiency_profile`. Down-and-distance splits such as third-and-short aren't recorded.

6. The Game Script & Official Prediction:
Conclude with a ## header outlining how the game will unfold across all four quarters.
Detail the turning point in the second half, identify the Super Bowl MVP archetype, and end with the bold projected scoreline:
**Projected Final: [Winner Name] [Score], [Loser Name] [Score]**

SUPER_BOWL_ROUNDTABLE_CONSENSUS.example_prompt_hook: Convene the expert roundtable for the Super Bowl. SUPER_BOWL_ROUNDTABLE_CONSENSUS.directive:
ARTICLE TYPE SPECIFICATION: The Bold Predictions & Panel Consensus
Granularity: Single-Game Pinnacle / Super Bowl Consensus.
Focus: Multi-voice expert roundtable, conflicting analytical models, bold prop/game predictions, and final scoreboard consensus.

SUPER_BOWL_ROUNDTABLE_CONSENSUS.curatorial_autonomy:
CURATORIAL AUTONOMY (THE ROUNDTABLE CONSENSUS):
This is a multi-voice feature designed to highlight conflicting models and narrative disagreements before the Super Bowl. You are acting as a panel of four distinct analysts. Do not have everyone agree.
- Analyst 1 (The Metrics/Tape Analyst like Kimes): Must base their prediction strictly on a schematic mismatch (e.g., pressure rates, coverage shells).
- Analyst 2 (The Contrarian like Acho): Must pick against the public consensus, citing a specific vulnerability in the favorite.
- Analyst 3 (The Narrativist like Simmons): Must focus on legacy, historical weight, and which team "needs it more."
- Analyst 4 (The Fantasy/Prop Expert like Yates): Must focus on a highly specific player prop or a volatile SpikeIndex player who will swing the game.
The panel must provide four distinct "Bold Predictions" that border on the extreme, followed by a final, official score prediction from each.
SUPER_BOWL_ROUNDTABLE_CONSENSUS.structure_directive:
ARTICLE STRUCTURE & FORMATTING DIRECTIVE:
Structure your article as an expert roundtable (approx. 1,000–1,200 words).

1. The Introduction (The Stakes):
Open with a headline using # (e.g., # Super Bowl LXI Predictions: Our Experts Call the Winner, the MVP, and the Game's Biggest Shock).
Write a 1-to-2 paragraph intro framing the clash of styles between the two teams and introducing the panel.

2. The Bold Predictions:
Use a ## header (e.g., ## The Bold Predictions).
Create four sub-sections using ### [Analyst Name's] Prediction: [The Prediction Kicker].
Each analyst gets exactly 1 paragraph (3–4 sentences) to make a hyper-specific, slightly outrageous claim about how the game unfolds (e.g., a defensive lineman winning MVP, a team being shut out in the first half, a specific trick play). They must write strictly in their assigned persona.

3. The X-Factor / MVP Picks:
Use a ## header (e.g., ## The Under-the-Radar MVP).
Use a bulleted list where each analyst names one player (outside of the starting QBs) who will dictate the outcome, tying it back to their specific analytical lens (e.g., SpikeIndex, Youth Production).

4. The Final Consensus (The Scoreboard):
Use a ## header (e.g., ## Official Super Bowl Picks).
List the final score prediction for each analyst in a clean format:
[Analyst Name]: [Winning Team] [Score], [Losing Team] [Score] (e.g., Mina Kimes: Chiefs 27, Eagles 24)
End the article with a single bolded line stating the overall panel consensus (e.g., **Panel Consensus: Chiefs 3-1**).

- Analyze how their individual SpikeIndex manifests on film: is their ceiling driven by rhythmic, anticipatory intermediate strikes or high-variance out-of-structure deep shots?
- Interrogate their efficiency against two-high shell rotations, evaluating whether they take underneath checkdowns or force high-risk throws into tight windows.
Focus entirely on the mechanical and mental execution required to win from the pocket.

COACHING DATA: Call `get_coach_profile` for both teams to know the front and man/zone lean each quarterback faces, and the `coaching_matchup` block of `get_matchup_edges` for the matchup itself. Tendencies are Low / Medium / High staff tendencies: describe them, never turn them into percentages or per-game counts.

SPLITS DATA: Call `get_player_scheme_splits` for both quarterbacks: how each handles strong pass rushes and coverages against his own average, set against the defense he faces (`get_matchup_edges`). Cite a split with its game count, as a tendency; if the tool's verdict says there aren't enough real games, leave splits out.
QUARTERBACK_DUEL_TAPE_BREAKDOWN.structure_directive:
ARTICLE STRUCTURE & FORMATTING DIRECTIVE:
Structure your piece as an in-depth coaching tape breakdown (approx. 1,000–1,300 words).

1. The Film Room Overture:
Open with a technical, film-study headline using # (e.g., # Inside the Film Room: Deconstructing the Super Bowl Quarterback Duel).
Write 2 paragraphs contrasting the mechanical styles and processing rhythms of the two signal-callers heading into the matchup.

2. Film Study: [Quarterback A] vs. Opposing Defensive Disguises:
Use a ## header focused on Quarterback A (e.g., ## [QB A Name]: Operating on Time vs. Simulated Pressures).
Break down his footwork, release point, and how he reads safety rotations post-snap. Detail the specific coverage shell (Cover 3 match, quarters, Cover 1 robber) the opposing defense will use to take away his primary read.

3. Film Study: [Quarterback B] vs. Opposing Defensive Disguises:
Use a ## header focused on Quarterback B (e.g., ## [QB B Name]: Pocket Navigation and Second-Reaction Creation).
Analyze how he handles edge and interior pressure paths. Detail whether his base breaks down under distress and how the opposing front seven can constrict his throwing lanes.

4. The High-Leverage Flashpoint: Third-and-Long & The Red Zone:
Use a ## header dissecting situational passing execution.
Contrast how both quarterbacks perform when the defense knows a pass is coming. Highlight each offense's third-down and red-zone rates and ranks from `get_team_efficiency_profile` and each quarterback's interceptions and sacks taken, then read red-zone throw placement into compressed coverage from there. Blitz, pressure and coverage splits aren't recorded; describe them as your read, never as numbers.

5. The Tape Room Verdict:
Conclude with a ### header naming the quarterback who possesses the technical and schematic edge to protect the football and execute the game-winning drive. End directly after the assessment without wrap-up filler.

SUPER_BOWL_MEDIA_INTERVIEW_AUDIT.name: The Super Bowl Media & Interview Audit (The Psychological Press Check)
SUPER_BOWL_MEDIA_INTERVIEW_AUDIT.granularity: Super Bowl Week / Media Availability & Narrative Arc
SUPER_BOWL_MEDIA_INTERVIEW_AUDIT.focus: Evaluating pre-game press conferences, Opening Night transcripts, locker room temperature, psychological pressure, and narrative control leading into the Super Bowl.
SUPER_BOWL_MEDIA_INTERVIEW_AUDIT.example_prompt_hook: Conduct a psychological press audit of Super Bowl week. Dissect the subtext of podium quotes, analyze quarterback body language under the microscope, isolate unforced errors for bulletin-board material, and determine which team won the media week.
SUPER_BOWL_MEDIA_INTERVIEW_AUDIT.directive:
ARTICLE TYPE SPECIFICATION: The Super Bowl Media & Interview Audit
Granularity: Super Bowl Week / Media Availability & Narrative Arc.
Focus: Podium psychology, locker room temperature, quote subtext, bulletin-board motivation, and narrative control.
Scope: Step away from on-field X's and O's. Conduct a rigorous psychological audit of Super Bowl media week. Analyze Opening Night transcripts, coach press conferences, and quarterback podium demeanor. Evaluate how both teams handle the pressure cooker without referencing betting spreads, moneylines, or contractual salaries.
SUPER_BOWL_MEDIA_INTERVIEW_AUDIT.curatorial_autonomy:
CURATORIAL AUTONOMY (MEDIA & PSYCHOLOGY AUDIT):
You are analyzing the pre-game press conferences, Opening Night transcripts, and media availability of the two Super Bowl teams. You are not writing a tactical breakdown. You are evaluating the psychological pressure, locker room temperature, and narrative control:
- Identify the overarching media narrative (e.g., "The veteran dynasty treating this like business as usual" vs. "The young upstarts overwhelmed by the lights").
- Analyze specific quotes for bulletin-board material, deflection of pressure, or subtle signs of anxiety.
- Evaluate how the head coaches are managing the media circus and shielding their rosters.
Select the defining psychological tension between the two franchises heading into Sunday.

COACHING DATA: Call `get_coach_profile` for both head coaches' tenure and playoff and Super Bowl experience when judging how each handles the media. Tendencies are Low / Medium / High staff tendencies: describe them, never turn them into percentages or per-game counts.
SUPER_BOWL_MEDIA_INTERVIEW_AUDIT.structure_directive:
ARTICLE STRUCTURE & FORMATTING DIRECTIVE:
Structure your article as a psychological and narrative audit of Super Bowl week (approx. 900–1,100 words).

1. The Temperature Check (The Hook):
Open with a headline using # (e.g., # Winning the Podium: Who Is Handling the Super Bowl Spotlight Better?).
Write a 2-paragraph introduction comparing the overall demeanor of the two franchises. Contrast their behavior against their historical Legacy Floor (e.g., a blue-blood franchise vs. a team making its first appearance in decades).

2. The Defining Quote (The Pivot Point):
Use a ## header (e.g., ## The Quote That Mattered).
Feature one specific, highly analyzed quote from a key figure (Coach, QB, or star player). Use blockquotes (>) for the quote itself.
Break down the subtext. Is it a sign of supreme confidence, a manufactured chip on their shoulder, or a subtle slip of frustration?

3. Quarterback Demeanor & The Weight of the Moment:
Use a ## header (e.g., ## The QBs Under the Microscope).
Contrast the media strategies of the two starting quarterbacks. Discuss how their Player Popularity Index and legacy stakes (e.g., first ring vs. dynasty building) are influencing their answers. Who is absorbing the pressure for their team?

4. Bulletin-Board Material & Unforced Errors:
Use a ## header (e.g., ## The Unforced Errors).
Highlight the assistant coach or supporting player who said too much. Analyze how the opposing locker room will use that soundbite for motivation.

5. The Final Read (The Verdict):
Conclude with a ### header summarizing which team definitively "won" the media week and whether their relaxed/focused demeanor will translate to the opening drive.

FRANCHISE_ARCHITECTURE_BLUEPRINT.name: The Franchise Architecture Blueprint (The Super Bowl Roster Build)
FRANCHISE_ARCHITECTURE_BLUEPRINT.focus: Forensic breakdown of how the two Super Bowl rosters were constructed, emphasizing positional resource allocation, draft pedigree yield, and youth production integration.
FRANCHISE_ARCHITECTURE_BLUEPRINT.example_prompt_hook: Deconstruct the roster architecture of the two Super Bowl finalists. Compare how both front offices allocated positional resources, maximized blue-chip draft capital, and integrated youth production to build a championship core.
FRANCHISE_ARCHITECTURE_BLUEPRINT.directive:
ARTICLE TYPE SPECIFICATION: The Franchise Architecture Blueprint
Granularity: Multi-Year / Foundational Roster Core.
Focus: Roster construction philosophies, positional resource allocation, draft capital yield, and youth vs. veteran deployment.
Scope: You are writing a definitive front-office breakdown of the two Super Bowl finalists during the bye week. Analyze how the two general managers constructed these rosters over the past 3-5 years. Rely on positional value, draft pedigree, and production efficiency rather than referencing specific player salary cap numbers or raw trade packages.
FRANCHISE_ARCHITECTURE_BLUEPRINT.curatorial_autonomy:
CURATORIAL AUTONOMY (ARCHITECTURE_BLUEPRINT):
You are analyzing the two Super Bowl teams exclusively through an executive lens. Do not preview the upcoming game's tactical matchups. Contrast their roster-building philosophies:
- Evaluate whether a team is powered by an overwhelming Blue-Chip Pedigree ($P_{\text{draft}}$) at premium positions or if they found undervalued efficiency on the margins.
- Assess the impact of Under-25 Production Share ($Y_{\text{prod}}$) in balancing their veteran core.
- Isolate the specific positional group (e.g., investing heavily in the defensive line versus stacking elite perimeter playmakers) that serves as the foundation for their respective title runs.
FRANCHISE_ARCHITECTURE_BLUEPRINT.structure_directive:
ARTICLE STRUCTURE & FORMATTING DIRECTIVE:
Structure your piece as a front-office deep dive (approx. 1,000–1,200 words).

1. The Executive Summary (The Hook):
Open with an authoritative headline using # (e.g., # Blueprint to the Lombardi: How the [Team A] and [Team B] Built Their Super Bowl Cores).
Write a 2-paragraph introduction framing the differing front-office philosophies of the two general managers and the distinct paths they took to the title game.

2. The Core Architecture: [AFC Champion Name]:
Use a ## header focused on the AFC team.
Detail their roster foundation. Highlight how they utilized high Blue-Chip Pedigree ($P_{\text{draft}}$) or integrated massive Under-25 Production ($Y_{\text{prod}}$) to build out their premium positions (Quarterback, Edge, Tackle, Corner).

3. The Core Architecture: [NFC Champion Name]:
Use a ## header focused on the NFC team.
Contrast their build with the AFC champion. If they lack high draft pedigree, explain how they maximized veteran Baseline Ratings ($R_{\text{rating}}$) and positional efficiency to cover up structural holes.

4. The Positional Value Disconnect:
Use a ## header (e.g., ## The Divergent Resource Allocation).
Identify the one specific position group where the two front offices took entirely different architectural approaches (e.g., Team A invested entirely in elite edge rushers, while Team B built the best secondary in football).

5. The Industry Takeaway:
Conclude with a ### header summarizing the primary roster-building lesson the rest of the league's 30 general managers must learn from these two finalists.

DRAFT_BLUEPRINT_ROSTER_AUDIT.name: The Draft Blueprint & Roster Core Audit (Picks 1–28)
DRAFT_BLUEPRINT_ROSTER_AUDIT.focus: Diagnostic audit of eliminated teams with locked draft picks (1–28), analyzing roster age curves, foundational core needs, and draft-capital mandates.
DRAFT_BLUEPRINT_ROSTER_AUDIT.example_prompt_hook: Audit the roster cores of eliminated playoff teams and lottery franchises. Define their primary draft mandate and diagnose which units require total overhauls.
DRAFT_BLUEPRINT_ROSTER_AUDIT.directive:
ARTICLE TYPE SPECIFICATION: The Draft Blueprint & Roster Core Audit
Granularity: Offseason / Multi-Year Core Audit.
Focus: Roster age curves, core unit stability, draft capital prioritization, and rebuild timelines.
Scope: Audit the structural health of teams locked into picks 1–28. Group teams by organizational status and define the exact positional blueprint they must execute in the draft without citing specific player salary numbers or speculative trades.
DRAFT_BLUEPRINT_ROSTER_AUDIT.curatorial_autonomy:
CURATORIAL AUTONOMY (DRAFT_BLUEPRINT):
You are evaluating the 28 eliminated franchises holding locked first-round draft capital.
- Pull `get_draft_order` for picks 1–28. After the Divisional round these picks are locked: each carries `locked` and `selection_status`. Cite only picks the tool marks locked, and never project picks 29–32, whose teams are still playing.
- Pull `get_advanced_team_analytics` and `get_team_draft_needs` for each franchise you consider.
Group the franchises into two distinct core diagnostics:
- Ascending youth cores: Under-25 Production ($Y_{\text{prod}}$) of 0.35 or higher, holding a high pick, that need an immediate blue-chip cornerstone to finish the build.
- Purgatory rosters: teams triggering the Purgatory Penalty, stuck with picks 12–20, that need a total identity reset rather than one more patch.
Select the 3 to 4 most urgent franchise blueprints to highlight in depth.
PROSPECT RULE: For each featured franchise you may name one or two real prospects at its top need, pulled from `get_scouted_draft_board` with its `position` filter. Never invent a prospect or name one who isn't on the board, and never fill in a field (height, weight, age, OVR, college) the board returns as null.
DRAFT_BLUEPRINT_ROSTER_AUDIT.structure_directive:
ARTICLE STRUCTURE & FORMATTING DIRECTIVE:
Structure your article as an executive roster blueprint (approx. 1,000–1,200 words).

1. The Offseason Landscape:
Open with a headline using # (e.g., # The Offseason Blueprint: Core Diagnostics and Draft Mandates for 28 Eliminated Rosters).
Write a 2-paragraph introduction framing the talent gap between the final four contenders and the rest of the league.

2. The Core Audits (3–4 Featured Franchises):
Use ## headers for each featured franchise (e.g., ## Dallas Cowboys: Escaping the Roster Purgatory Trap).
For each team, state its exact locked pick number from `get_draft_order` and its top 3 positional needs from `get_team_draft_needs`, in ranked order. Then evaluate their foundational core: cite their youth production share and draft pedigree, and say which core diagnostic (ascending youth core or Purgatory reset) they fall into. Specify their primary positional mandate for April; if you name a prospect at the top need, use only one or two from the scouted board.

3. Macro Positional Scarcity:
Use a ## header evaluating which position group is in highest demand across the eliminated 28 teams.

4. The Mandate:
Conclude with a ### header declaring the single front office facing the most consequential draft weekend in franchise history.

OFFSEASON_MOCK_DRAFT.directive:

Prioritize premium positional value (QB, OT, EDGE, CB, the $M_{\text{pos}}$ multipliers) over low-impact positions, balanced against team needs. Use each roster's Under-25 Production Share ($Y_{\text{prod}}$) to judge whether an organization needs an immediate foundational starter or can afford a developmental high-ceiling prospect.
OFFSEASON_MOCK_DRAFT.structure_directive:
ARTICLE STRUCTURE & FORMATTING DIRECTIVE:
Structure your piece as an authoritative Mock Draft (approx. 1,500–1,800 words).

1. The Board Overview:
Open with a headline using # (e.g., # 2036 NFL Mock Draft 1.0: First-Round Projections for Picks 1–24).
Write a 2-paragraph introduction identifying the strengths of this draft class and the run on premium positions.

Use numbered ## headers for each selection formatted strictly as: ## [Pick Number]. [Team Name]: [Prospect Name], [Position], [School] (e.g., ## 1. Philadelphia Eagles: Dave Vogel, LEDG, Georgia), taking the name, position and school exactly from the board.

FANTASY_DRAFT_TIERS.name: Fantasy Draft Tiers
FANTASY_DRAFT_TIERS.focus: Tiered draft rankings for one position (assigned by the desk), built from the preseason draft board.

Group players into 5 to 7 tiers where the drop-off is real, not every 12 picks. Use ADP and its range to show where each player actually goes, and depth-chart role, age, experience and his offense's strength to argue where he should go. Call out at least two players you would take earlier than their ADP and two you would let someone else draft.
FANTASY_DRAFT_TIERS.structure_directive:
ARTICLE STRUCTURE & FORMATTING DIRECTIVE:
Structure the article as a positional draft tier guide (at least 1,300 words; longer is fine when the content earns it).

1. The Positional Thesis:
Open with a headline using #. Write 1–2 paragraphs on how this position shapes drafts this year: where the elite tier ends, how deep it runs, and the round where value falls off.

2. The Tiers:
Use ## headers for each tier with a name and pick range (e.g., ## Tier 2: The Weekly Difference-Makers (Picks 10–24)).
Under each, one short paragraph on what the tier has in common, then list each player in bold with team, ADP and range, followed by 1–2 sentences on his case.

A ## section with my reaches (players to take before their ADP) and my fades (players to let go), each with the reason.

End after the Draft Day Calls.
FANTASY_DRAFT_TIERS.directive:
ARTICLE TYPE SPECIFICATION: Fantasy Draft Tiers
Granularity: Preseason / One Position.
Focus: Tiered draft rankings for one position (assigned by the desk), built from the preseason draft board.
Scope: One position only. Tier every draftable player at it, with ADP, range and a case for each.
FANTASY_DRAFT_TIERS.example_prompt_hook: Tier this year's draft board at your assigned position. Show where the real drop-offs are, where each player goes on average, and which players you'd reach for or let fall.

FANTASY_SLEEPERS_BUSTS.name: Fantasy Sleepers & Busts
FANTASY_SLEEPERS_BUSTS.focus: Players whose draft cost doesn't match their likely role: sleepers going too late and busts going too early.
FANTASY_SLEEPERS_BUSTS.curatorial_autonomy:

Scan the whole draft board. A sleeper is a player whose depth-chart role, offense or youth points to more than his ADP (a starter going in round 10, a young player who just moved up the depth chart). A bust is a player whose ADP assumes more than his role supports (a backup priced like a starter, a veteran on a weak offense). Pick 6 to 8 sleepers and 5 to 6 busts across positions; include at least one sleeper drafted in fewer than half of leagues.
FANTASY_SLEEPERS_BUSTS.structure_directive:
ARTICLE STRUCTURE & FORMATTING DIRECTIVE:
Structure the article as a sleepers-and-busts column (at least 1,100 words; longer is fine when the content earns it).

1. Open with a headline using # and a short paragraph on where this draft board is most wrong.
2. ## Sleepers: each player in bold with team, position, ADP and range, then 2–3 sentences on the role or situation the market is missing.
3. ## Busts: same format, explaining what the ADP assumes and why the role doesn't support it.
4. ## The One I'd Bet On: a single closing paragraph naming your favorite sleeper and the round you'd take him.
FANTASY_SLEEPERS_BUSTS.directive:
ARTICLE TYPE SPECIFICATION: Fantasy Sleepers & Busts
Granularity: Preseason / Full Board.
Focus: Players whose draft cost doesn't match their likely role: sleepers going too late and busts going too early.
Scope: Cross-position. 6–8 sleepers and 5–6 busts, each argued from role versus draft cost.
FANTASY_SLEEPERS_BUSTS.example_prompt_hook: Find the players the draft market has wrong: the starters going too late and the names going too early, and tell readers where to take or avoid them.

FANTASY_MOCK_DRAFT.name: Fantasy Mock Draft

Compare notable picks with ADP.
FANTASY_MOCK_DRAFT.structure_directive:

FANTASY_MOCK_DRAFT.directive:
ARTICLE TYPE SPECIFICATION: Fantasy Mock Draft
Granularity: Preseason / One 12-Team Draft.
Focus: A pick-by-pick write-up of one 12-team PPR mock draft, with each team's approach.
Scope: One simulated 12-team draft. Rounds 1–5 pick by pick, the rest by team.
FANTASY_MOCK_DRAFT.example_prompt_hook: Walk through a 12-team PPR mock draft pick by pick, explain each team's approach, and grade the rosters that came out of it.

FANTASY_ROOKIE_RANKINGS.focus: Rankings of rookies only (no prior NFL experience) for redraft leagues, by role and draft cost.

FANTASY_ROOKIE_RANKINGS.structure_directive:
ARTICLE STRUCTURE & FORMATTING DIRECTIVE:
Structure the article as a rookie ranking list (at least 1,000 words; longer is fine when the content earns it).

2. ## The Rankings: numbered list; each rookie in bold with team, position, ADP and draft %, then 1–2 sentences on role and outlook.

FANTASY_ROOKIE_RANKINGS.directive:
ARTICLE TYPE SPECIFICATION: Fantasy Rookie Rankings
Granularity: Preseason / Rookies.
Focus: Rankings of rookies only (no prior NFL experience) for redraft leagues, by role and draft cost.
Scope: Rookies only (0 years of experience). Top 15–20 by redraft value.
FANTASY_ROOKIE_RANKINGS.example_prompt_hook: Rank this year's rookies for fantasy drafts: who starts right away, who's one move from a role, and who's only a late flier.

FANTASY_START_SIT.name: Start 'Em, Sit 'Em
FANTASY_START_SIT.focus: The week's lineup calls by position: who to start and who to sit, beyond the obvious every-week starters.
FANTASY_START_SIT.curatorial_autonomy:

Pull this week's rankings for each position with get_fantasy_rankings. Skip players everyone starts no matter what (the top few at each position) unless there's a real reason to worry. Focus on the decisions managers actually face: players ranked around the line between starter and bench, and players started in most leagues who shouldn't be (or started in few who should). For each call, use at least two of: this week's projection and rank, recent production, usage trend, and the matchup. Note teams on bye.

SPLITS DATA: Call `get_player_scheme_splits` for close calls: a player's production against defenses like this week's opponent (Strong / Average / Weak scoring defense, pass rush, coverage). Cite a split with its game count, as a tendency; if the tool's verdict says there aren't enough real games, leave splits out.
FANTASY_START_SIT.structure_directive:
ARTICLE STRUCTURE & FORMATTING DIRECTIVE:
Structure the article as a Start 'Em, Sit 'Em column (at least 1,300 words; longer is fine when the content earns it).

1. Open with a headline using # (include the week) and 1–2 paragraphs setting up the week: byes, the biggest decision, one bad call of yours from last week if there is one.
2. ## Quarterbacks, ## Running Backs, ## Wide Receivers, ## Tight Ends: under each, ### Start 'Em (2–3 players) and ### Sit 'Em (2–3 players). Each player in bold with team and opponent, then 2–3 sentences with the numbers behind the call.

In playoff and championship editions, frame every call around winning this one game.
FANTASY_START_SIT.directive:
ARTICLE TYPE SPECIFICATION: Start 'Em, Sit 'Em
Granularity: Week-level / Lineup Calls.
Focus: The week's lineup calls by position: who to start and who to sit, beyond the obvious every-week starters.

FANTASY_WAIVER_WIRE.name: Waiver Wire

FANTASY_WAIVER_WIRE.structure_directive:
ARTICLE STRUCTURE & FORMATTING DIRECTIVE:

4. ## Safe to Drop: one player and why.
FANTASY_WAIVER_WIRE.directive:
ARTICLE TYPE SPECIFICATION: Waiver Wire
Granularity: Week-level / Pickups.
Focus: The week's best pickups by position, ordered by priority, with how widely each player is rostered.

FANTASY_WAIVER_WIRE.example_prompt_hook: Rank this week's waiver pickups: who to claim first, how widely each is rostered, and whether the breakout is built on real volume.

FANTASY_WEEKLY_REACTIONS.name: Weekly Fantasy Reactions
FANTASY_WEEKLY_REACTIONS.focus: Reactions to last week's fantasy results: the booms, the busts and what changed.
FANTASY_WEEKLY_REACTIONS.curatorial_autonomy:
CURATORIAL AUTONOMY (WEEKLY FANTASY REACTIONS):
Use get_fantasy_week_results for last week (top scorers, biggest beats and misses against projection). Pick 8 to 10 storylines: the week's best performances, the most painful busts among players most managers started, and any usage change that matters going forward.
