FANTASY_WEEKLY_REACTIONS.structure_directive:
ARTICLE STRUCTURE & FORMATTING DIRECTIVE:
Structure the article as a weekly reactions column (at least 1,100 words; longer is fine when the content earns it).

1. Open with a headline using # (include the week recapped) and a paragraph on the story of the fantasy week.
2. ## Booms: 4–5 players in bold with team, points scored versus projection and the stat line, then whether it repeats.
3. ## Busts: 3–4 players, same format, and whether to worry.
4. ## What Changed: 1–2 usage or role shifts that matter for next week.
5. Close with one line on how you'd react in your own league.
FANTASY_WEEKLY_REACTIONS.directive:
ARTICLE TYPE SPECIFICATION: Weekly Fantasy Reactions
Granularity: Week-level / Last Week's Results.
Focus: Reactions to last week's fantasy results: the booms, the busts and what changed.
Scope: Last week only. 8–10 storylines, each judged as a blip or a real change.
FANTASY_WEEKLY_REACTIONS.example_prompt_hook: React to last week's fantasy results: the big games, the painful busts against projection, and which ones actually change anything.

FANTASY_RANKINGS_TIERS.name: Weekly Rankings & Tiers
FANTASY_RANKINGS_TIERS.focus: This week's QB, RB, WR and TE rankings grouped into tiers.
FANTASY_RANKINGS_TIERS.curatorial_autonomy:
CURATORIAL AUTONOMY (WEEKLY RANKINGS & TIERS):
Pull this week's rankings at each position with get_fantasy_rankings (about 15 QBs and TEs, 30 RBs and WRs). Group each position into 4 to 5 tiers where the projections show a real gap. You may move a player up or down a tier from the projection order when usage, matchup or recent form justifies it; say so when you do.
FANTASY_RANKINGS_TIERS.structure_directive:
ARTICLE STRUCTURE & FORMATTING DIRECTIVE:
Structure the article as weekly tiered rankings (at least 1,200 words; longer is fine when the content earns it).

1. Open with a headline using # (include the week) and a short paragraph on the week's biggest ranking stories and byes.
2. ## Quarterbacks, ## Running Backs, ## Wide Receivers, ## Tight Ends: for each, ### Tier 1 … ### Tier 5 with a one-line tier description, then players in rank order as 'Rank. Player (Team) vs/@ Opponent, projection' with a short note only where you moved a player off the projection order.
FANTASY_RANKINGS_TIERS.directive:
ARTICLE TYPE SPECIFICATION: Weekly Rankings & Tiers
Granularity: Week-level / All Positions.
Focus: This week's QB, RB, WR and TE rankings grouped into tiers.
Scope: All four positions, tiered, for this week only.
FANTASY_RANKINGS_TIERS.example_prompt_hook: Tier this week's rankings at every position, and flag the players you'd move off the projection order.

FANTASY_BOX_SCORE_USAGE.name: Box Score Breakdown & Usage
FANTASY_BOX_SCORE_USAGE.focus: Who is getting the ball: carries, receptions and team shares from last week's box scores, and the usage trends behind them.
FANTASY_BOX_SCORE_USAGE.curatorial_autonomy:
CURATORIAL AUTONOMY (BOX SCORE BREAKDOWN & USAGE):
Use get_fantasy_usage league-wide for touch risers and fallers, then team by team for the most interesting backfields and receiving corps. Cover 8 to 10 teams where usage changed or where the split matters for fantasy decisions. Separate volume (carries, receptions, share of the team's touches) from efficiency (points per touch).
FANTASY_BOX_SCORE_USAGE.structure_directive:
ARTICLE STRUCTURE & FORMATTING DIRECTIVE:
Structure the article as a usage breakdown (at least 1,100 words; longer is fine when the content earns it).

1. Open with a headline using # (include the week) and a paragraph on the week's biggest usage shift.
2. ## Rising Usage and ## Falling Usage: 3–4 players each, in bold with team, the last three games' carries/receptions and team share against the rest of the season.
3. ## Team Splits to Watch: 3–4 teams, one short paragraph each on how the work is divided.
4. End with ## Usage Calls: one-line add/start/sell notes.
FANTASY_BOX_SCORE_USAGE.directive:
ARTICLE TYPE SPECIFICATION: Box Score Breakdown & Usage
Granularity: Week-level / Volume by Team.
Focus: Who is getting the ball: carries, receptions and team shares from last week's box scores, and the usage trends behind them.
Scope: League-wide usage trends plus 3–4 team splits.
FANTASY_BOX_SCORE_USAGE.example_prompt_hook: Break down who's getting the ball: the usage risers and fallers and the team splits that decide fantasy lineups.

FANTASY_TEN_THINGS.name: 10 Things to Know This Week
FANTASY_TEN_THINGS.focus: A numbered preview of ten things fantasy managers need to know before this week's games.
FANTASY_TEN_THINGS.curatorial_autonomy:
CURATORIAL AUTONOMY (10 THINGS TO KNOW THIS WEEK):
Pick ten distinct items for this week: byes and who they hurt, the best and worst matchups, a usage trend, a projection that surprises you, a widely started player to worry about, a lightly started one to trust. Mix positions, and don't repeat the same player.
FANTASY_TEN_THINGS.structure_directive:
ARTICLE STRUCTURE & FORMATTING DIRECTIVE:
Structure the article as a numbered preview list (at least 900 words; longer is fine when the content earns it).

1. Open with a headline using # (include the week) and a 2–3 sentence intro.
2. Ten items as ## 1. … ## 10., each with a bold one-line takeaway and a short paragraph with the numbers.
3. No closing section after item 10.
FANTASY_TEN_THINGS.directive:
ARTICLE TYPE SPECIFICATION: 10 Things to Know This Week
Granularity: Week-level / Preview List.
Focus: A numbered preview of ten things fantasy managers need to know before this week's games.
Scope: Ten distinct, forward-looking items for this week.
FANTASY_TEN_THINGS.example_prompt_hook: Give fantasy managers ten things to know before this week's games: byes, matchups, usage and the projections that surprise you.

FANTASY_MATCHUP_EXPLOITS.name: Matchup Exploits
FANTASY_MATCHUP_EXPLOITS.focus: This week's best and worst fantasy matchups by position: defenses to attack and defenses to avoid.
FANTASY_MATCHUP_EXPLOITS.curatorial_autonomy:
CURATORIAL AUTONOMY (MATCHUP EXPLOITS):
Use get_fantasy_defense_vs_position (season and last four games) with this week's schedule from get_fantasy_rankings. For each position, name the two most exploitable matchups and the one to avoid, and the specific players affected. Prefer defenses whose last four games agree with their season numbers; say when they don't.

SPLITS DATA: Call `get_player_scheme_splits` to back a matchup call with how the player has done against defenses of the same kind. Cite a split with its game count, as a tendency; if the tool's verdict says there aren't enough real games, leave splits out.
FANTASY_MATCHUP_EXPLOITS.structure_directive:
ARTICLE STRUCTURE & FORMATTING DIRECTIVE:
Structure the article as a matchup column (at least 900 words; longer is fine when the content earns it).

1. Open with a headline using # (include the week) and a paragraph on the week's best matchup.
2. ## Quarterbacks, ## Running Backs, ## Wide Receivers, ## Tight Ends: ### Attack (2 matchups) and ### Avoid (1), naming the defense, what it allows per game, and the players to start or bench because of it.
FANTASY_MATCHUP_EXPLOITS.directive:
ARTICLE TYPE SPECIFICATION: Matchup Exploits
Granularity: Week-level / Matchups by Position.
Focus: This week's best and worst fantasy matchups by position: defenses to attack and defenses to avoid.
Scope: All four positions; 2 matchups to attack and 1 to avoid each.
FANTASY_MATCHUP_EXPLOITS.example_prompt_hook: Find this week's matchups to exploit and avoid at every position, and name the players they help or hurt.

FANTASY_DVP_REPORT.name: Defense vs. Position Report
FANTASY_DVP_REPORT.focus: The season-level picture of which defenses give up fantasy points to each position, and which of those numbers are real.
FANTASY_DVP_REPORT.curatorial_autonomy:
CURATORIAL AUTONOMY (DEFENSE VS. POSITION REPORT):
Use get_fantasy_defense_vs_position for all positions. For each position, identify the three most generous and three stingiest defenses, and point out where the last four games disagree with the season (a defense getting better or worse). Explain what it means for the coming weeks of schedules.
FANTASY_DVP_REPORT.structure_directive:
ARTICLE STRUCTURE & FORMATTING DIRECTIVE:
Structure the article as a defense-vs-position report (at least 1,000 words; longer is fine when the content earns it).

1. Open with a headline using # and a paragraph on the most surprising defensive trend.
2. ## Quarterbacks, ## Running Backs, ## Wide Receivers, ## Tight Ends: the most generous and stingiest defenses with points allowed per game (season and last four), and one sentence on what's driving each.
3. ## Trends to Trust: 2–3 defenses whose recent games change the picture.
FANTASY_DVP_REPORT.directive:
ARTICLE TYPE SPECIFICATION: Defense vs. Position Report
Granularity: Season-to-date / Defenses.
Focus: The season-level picture of which defenses give up fantasy points to each position, and which of those numbers are real.
Scope: Season-to-date defense vs. position, with recent trends.
FANTASY_DVP_REPORT.example_prompt_hook: Map which defenses are giving up fantasy points to each position, which numbers are real, and what it means for upcoming schedules.

FANTASY_OVERREACTION_CHECK.name: Overreaction Check
FANTASY_OVERREACTION_CHECK.focus: Hot and cold starts tested against usage and role: what's real and what's noise.
FANTASY_OVERREACTION_CHECK.curatorial_autonomy:
CURATORIAL AUTONOMY (OVERREACTION CHECK):
Pick 6 to 8 of the season's loudest early storylines (big starts and slow starts among highly drafted players). For each, compare points with usage and role: is a hot start built on touches, or on touchdowns and one long play? Is a slow start bad luck on solid volume, or a lost role? Give each a verdict: Real, Mostly Real, Noise.
FANTASY_OVERREACTION_CHECK.structure_directive:
ARTICLE STRUCTURE & FORMATTING DIRECTIVE:
Structure the article as an overreaction column (at least 1,100 words; longer is fine when the content earns it).

1. Open with a headline using # and a paragraph on the dangers of early samples.
2. One ## section per storyline phrased as the overreaction (e.g., ## 'Player X is a league-winner'), with the evidence and a bold verdict line: **Verdict: Real / Mostly Real / Noise**.
3. Close with ## The One I'm Buying: a single paragraph.
FANTASY_OVERREACTION_CHECK.directive:
ARTICLE TYPE SPECIFICATION: Overreaction Check
Granularity: Early season / Small Samples.
Focus: Hot and cold starts tested against usage and role: what's real and what's noise.
Scope: 6–8 early-season storylines, each judged Real, Mostly Real or Noise.
FANTASY_OVERREACTION_CHECK.example_prompt_hook: Test the season's loudest early fantasy storylines against usage and role, and tell readers which are real and which are noise.

FANTASY_BUY_SELL.name: Trade Targets: Buy & Sell
FANTASY_BUY_SELL.focus: Players to trade for and trade away, based on the gap between production and the usage and schedule behind it.
FANTASY_BUY_SELL.curatorial_autonomy:
CURATORIAL AUTONOMY (TRADE TARGETS: BUY & SELL):
Use rest-of-season rankings (get_fantasy_rankings with sort='ros'), season scoring profiles and usage. Buy players whose usage and remaining schedule are better than their recent points; sell players whose points have outrun their touches or whose schedule turns. Pick 4 to 5 buys and 4 to 5 sells across positions, with a realistic trade idea for at least two. Players rostered in most leagues are the trade market; don't list free agents.
FANTASY_BUY_SELL.structure_directive:
ARTICLE STRUCTURE & FORMATTING DIRECTIVE:
Structure the article as a trade column (at least 1,100 words; longer is fine when the content earns it).

1. Open with a headline using # and a paragraph on the state of the trade market.
2. ## Buy: each player in bold with team, the case (usage, projection, schedule) and what you'd offer.
3. ## Sell: same format, with what you'd ask for.
4. ## Hold: 1–2 players everyone is asking about who aren't worth moving.
FANTASY_BUY_SELL.directive:
ARTICLE TYPE SPECIFICATION: Trade Targets: Buy & Sell
Granularity: Midseason / Trade Targets.
Focus: Players to trade for and trade away, based on the gap between production and the usage and schedule behind it.
Scope: 4–5 buys and 4–5 sells among rostered players, with trade ideas.
FANTASY_BUY_SELL.example_prompt_hook: Name the players to buy and sell before their value changes, built on the gap between production and the usage behind it.

FANTASY_ADP_CHECKPOINT.name: ADP Checkpoint
FANTASY_ADP_CHECKPOINT.focus: How draft-day prices compare with value so far: who has beaten their ADP and who has fallen short.
FANTASY_ADP_CHECKPOINT.curatorial_autonomy:
CURATORIAL AUTONOMY (ADP CHECKPOINT):
Use get_fantasy_draft_board (it shows season points and positional finish so far next to ADP) and rest-of-season rankings. Pick the biggest values (late picks finishing high) and the biggest disappointments (early picks finishing low), and say whether each gap will keep going or close over the rest of the season.
FANTASY_ADP_CHECKPOINT.structure_directive:
ARTICLE STRUCTURE & FORMATTING DIRECTIVE:
Structure the article as a midseason draft checkpoint (at least 1,000 words; longer is fine when the content earns it).

1. Open with a headline using # and a paragraph on what this year's draft got right and wrong.
2. ## Beating Their ADP: 4–5 players in bold with ADP, current positional finish and rest-of-season outlook.
3. ## Falling Short: 4–5 players, same format.
4. ## If We Redrafted Today: a short ranked list of the top 10.
FANTASY_ADP_CHECKPOINT.directive:
ARTICLE TYPE SPECIFICATION: ADP Checkpoint
Granularity: Midseason / Draft Cost vs. Value.
Focus: How draft-day prices compare with value so far: who has beaten their ADP and who has fallen short.
Scope: ADP versus production so far, plus a redraft top 10.
FANTASY_ADP_CHECKPOINT.example_prompt_hook: Check this year's draft prices against what players have delivered, and say which gaps will last.

FANTASY_ROS_TIERS.name: Rest-of-Season Tiers
FANTASY_ROS_TIERS.focus: Rest-of-season rankings by position, grouped into tiers, including the fantasy playoff schedule.
FANTASY_ROS_TIERS.curatorial_autonomy:
CURATORIAL AUTONOMY (REST-OF-SEASON TIERS):
Use get_fantasy_rankings with sort='ros' for each position and the playoff schedule view of get_fantasy_defense_vs_position. Tier the top 12 QBs and TEs and top 24 RBs and WRs for the rest of the season. Note each player's Weeks 15–17 schedule when it moves him within a tier.
FANTASY_ROS_TIERS.structure_directive:
ARTICLE STRUCTURE & FORMATTING DIRECTIVE:
Structure the article as rest-of-season tiers (at least 1,200 words; longer is fine when the content earns it).

1. Open with a headline using # and a paragraph on how the rest-of-season picture has changed.
2. ## Quarterbacks, ## Running Backs, ## Wide Receivers, ## Tight Ends: ### Tier headers, players in order with team, rest-of-season projection and a short note on schedule or role.
FANTASY_ROS_TIERS.directive:
ARTICLE TYPE SPECIFICATION: Rest-of-Season Tiers
Granularity: Rest of season / All Positions.
Focus: Rest-of-season rankings by position, grouped into tiers, including the fantasy playoff schedule.
Scope: Rest-of-season tiers at all four positions, with playoff schedule notes.
FANTASY_ROS_TIERS.example_prompt_hook: Tier every position for the rest of the season, with the fantasy playoff schedule factored in.

FANTASY_TRADE_DEADLINE_SPECIAL.name: Trade Deadline Special
FANTASY_TRADE_DEADLINE_SPECIAL.granularity: Week 12 / Last Call Before the Deadline
FANTASY_TRADE_DEADLINE_SPECIAL.focus: Final trade moves before the fantasy trade deadline (before Week 12 kickoff), weighted toward the playoff schedule.
FANTASY_TRADE_DEADLINE_SPECIAL.curatorial_autonomy:
CURATORIAL AUTONOMY (TRADE DEADLINE SPECIAL):
This is the last week to trade. Combine rest-of-season value with Weeks 15–17 schedules (playoff schedule view of get_fantasy_defense_vs_position). Write for two kinds of teams: contenders (trade depth for a playoff-week difference-maker) and teams on the bubble (buy cheap volume to make the playoffs). Include 4–5 buys, 4–5 sells and two concrete trade packages.
FANTASY_TRADE_DEADLINE_SPECIAL.structure_directive:
ARTICLE STRUCTURE & FORMATTING DIRECTIVE:
Structure the article as a deadline column (at least 1,200 words; longer is fine when the content earns it).

1. Open with a headline using # and a paragraph on why this deadline matters.
2. ## For Contenders and ## For Bubble Teams: buys and sells for each, in bold with team and the case.
3. ## Two Trades I'd Make: two specific packages with the reasoning.
4. ## Don't Overthink It: one closing paragraph.
FANTASY_TRADE_DEADLINE_SPECIAL.directive:
ARTICLE TYPE SPECIFICATION: Trade Deadline Special
Granularity: Week 12 / Last Call Before the Deadline.
Focus: Final trade moves before the fantasy trade deadline (before Week 12 kickoff), weighted toward the playoff schedule.
Scope: Last trade window: buys, sells and two trade packages, split by team situation.
FANTASY_TRADE_DEADLINE_SPECIAL.example_prompt_hook: It's the last week to trade: tell contenders and bubble teams exactly which players to buy and sell for the fantasy playoffs.

FANTASY_PLAYOFF_SCHEDULE_PLANNER.name: Fantasy Playoff Schedule Planner
FANTASY_PLAYOFF_SCHEDULE_PLANNER.focus: Weeks 15–17 schedules by position: who to stash, start and avoid for the fantasy playoffs.
FANTASY_PLAYOFF_SCHEDULE_PLANNER.curatorial_autonomy:
CURATORIAL AUTONOMY (FANTASY PLAYOFF SCHEDULE PLANNER):
Use the playoff schedule view of get_fantasy_defense_vs_position at each position. Name the offenses with the easiest and hardest Weeks 15–17 schedules for each position and the specific players affected, plus 3–4 waiver stashes with friendly playoff schedules. In Week 15, write only for teams that made the playoffs.
FANTASY_PLAYOFF_SCHEDULE_PLANNER.structure_directive:
ARTICLE STRUCTURE & FORMATTING DIRECTIVE:
Structure the article as a playoff planner (at least 1,000 words; longer is fine when the content earns it).

1. Open with a headline using # and a paragraph on the playoff schedule's biggest winners.
2. ## Quarterbacks, ## Running Backs, ## Wide Receivers, ## Tight Ends: ### Best Schedules and ### Worst Schedules, naming the Week 15, 16 and 17 opponents and what they allow.
3. ## Playoff Stashes: 3–4 lightly rostered players with friendly schedules.
FANTASY_PLAYOFF_SCHEDULE_PLANNER.directive:
ARTICLE TYPE SPECIFICATION: Fantasy Playoff Schedule Planner
Granularity: Weeks 15–17 / Schedules by Position.
Focus: Weeks 15–17 schedules by position: who to stash, start and avoid for the fantasy playoffs.
Scope: Weeks 15–17 schedules at all four positions, plus playoff stashes.
FANTASY_PLAYOFF_SCHEDULE_PLANNER.example_prompt_hook: Plan for the fantasy playoffs: which schedules are friendly in Weeks 15–17, who to stash, and who to worry about.

FANTASY_MUST_WIN_WEEK.name: Must-Win Week
FANTASY_MUST_WIN_WEEK.focus: Advice for teams on the fantasy playoff bubble in the last week of the regular season.
FANTASY_MUST_WIN_WEEK.curatorial_autonomy:
CURATORIAL AUTONOMY (MUST-WIN WEEK):
Week 14 decides playoff spots. Write for managers who need a win: high-floor starts at each position (players with steady points and few bad weeks), one-week adds with good matchups, and the risky players to bench when you only need a solid score. Also give a short note to teams already in: rest nothing, but plan for Week 15.
FANTASY_MUST_WIN_WEEK.structure_directive:
ARTICLE STRUCTURE & FORMATTING DIRECTIVE:
Structure the article as a must-win column (at least 1,000 words; longer is fine when the content earns it).

1. Open with a headline using # and a paragraph to the managers on the bubble.
2. ## Safe Starts: 1–2 high-floor players per position with their scoring range.
3. ## One-Week Adds: 3–4 lightly rostered players with friendly matchups.
4. ## Bench the Boom-or-Bust: 2–3 volatile players.
5. ## Already In?: a short paragraph looking ahead to Week 15.
FANTASY_MUST_WIN_WEEK.directive:
ARTICLE TYPE SPECIFICATION: Must-Win Week
Granularity: Week 14 / Last Regular-Season Week.
Focus: Advice for teams on the fantasy playoff bubble in the last week of the regular season.
Scope: Week 14 only: floor-first advice for teams that must win.
FANTASY_MUST_WIN_WEEK.example_prompt_hook: It's the last week of the fantasy regular season: give bubble teams the safe starts, one-week adds and risky players to bench.

FANTASY_PLAYOFF_STREAMERS.name: Playoff Streamers
FANTASY_PLAYOFF_STREAMERS.focus: One-week pickups for the fantasy playoffs, based on this week's matchups and projections.
FANTASY_PLAYOFF_STREAMERS.curatorial_autonomy:
CURATORIAL AUTONOMY (PLAYOFF STREAMERS):
Only this week matters. Use get_fantasy_waiver_wire with a higher max_rostered_pct if needed and this week's rankings. Recommend 2–3 streamers per position, ranked by this week's projection and matchup, with rostered %. Nothing about rest-of-season value.

SPLITS DATA: Call `get_player_scheme_splits` for a streamer's production against defenses like his playoff-week opponent. Cite a split with its game count, as a tendency; if the tool's verdict says there aren't enough real games, leave splits out.
FANTASY_PLAYOFF_STREAMERS.structure_directive:
ARTICLE STRUCTURE & FORMATTING DIRECTIVE:
Structure the article as a streaming list (at least 800 words; longer is fine when the content earns it).

1. Open with a headline using # (include the playoff round) and a 2–3 sentence intro.
2. ## Quarterbacks, ## Running Backs, ## Wide Receivers, ## Tight Ends: numbered streamers in bold with team, opponent, rostered % and projection, then one sentence each.
3. ## Deepest Dive: one player rostered in very few leagues.
FANTASY_PLAYOFF_STREAMERS.directive:
ARTICLE TYPE SPECIFICATION: Playoff Streamers
Granularity: Playoff week / One-Week Pickups.
Focus: One-week pickups for the fantasy playoffs, based on this week's matchups and projections.
Scope: This week only: 2–3 streamers per position.
FANTASY_PLAYOFF_STREAMERS.example_prompt_hook: Find this playoff week's best one-week pickups at every position, built only on this week's matchup and projection.

FANTASY_CEILING_PLAYS.name: Ceiling Plays & Safe Floors
FANTASY_CEILING_PLAYS.focus: How to build a playoff lineup depending on whether you're the favorite or the underdog: safe floors versus high ceilings.
FANTASY_CEILING_PLAYS.curatorial_autonomy:
CURATORIAL AUTONOMY (CEILING PLAYS & SAFE FLOORS):
Favorites should start steady players; underdogs need players who can win the week on their own. Use season scoring profiles (best, worst, spread, boom and bust weeks) with this week's projections. Name 6–8 high-ceiling players and 6–8 safe floors across positions, and give 2–3 swap decisions (Player A for the safe floor, Player B if you're behind).
FANTASY_CEILING_PLAYS.structure_directive:
ARTICLE STRUCTURE & FORMATTING DIRECTIVE:
Structure the article as a strategy column (at least 1,000 words; longer is fine when the content earns it).

1. Open with a headline using # and a paragraph on why variance matters in a single-elimination week.
2. ## If You're the Favorite: Safe Floors (players with their scoring range and why).
3. ## If You're the Underdog: Ceiling Plays (same format).
4. ## Close Calls: 2–3 either-or decisions resolved for both situations.
FANTASY_CEILING_PLAYS.directive:
ARTICLE TYPE SPECIFICATION: Ceiling Plays & Safe Floors
Granularity: Playoff week / Risk Management.
Focus: How to build a playoff lineup depending on whether you're the favorite or the underdog: safe floors versus high ceilings.
Scope: Floors for favorites, ceilings for underdogs, with swap decisions.
FANTASY_CEILING_PLAYS.example_prompt_hook: Build a playoff lineup for your situation: steady floors if you're favored, big ceilings if you're the underdog.

FANTASY_SEASON_IN_REVIEW.name: Fantasy Season in Review
FANTASY_SEASON_IN_REVIEW.focus: The fantasy season told as a story: the storylines, breakouts and collapses that decided leagues.
FANTASY_SEASON_IN_REVIEW.curatorial_autonomy:
CURATORIAL AUTONOMY (FANTASY SEASON IN REVIEW):
Tell the story of the fantasy season (Weeks 1–17) through 5 to 7 storylines: the players who won leagues, the early picks who sank teams, the in-season breakouts, the playoff weeks that decided titles. Use season and playoff leaders, the draft board's ADP against finish, and player profiles. No awards and no ranked lists: that's the Awards article.
FANTASY_SEASON_IN_REVIEW.structure_directive:
ARTICLE STRUCTURE & FORMATTING DIRECTIVE:
Structure the article as a narrative season review (at least 1,300 words; longer is fine when the content earns it).

1. Open with a headline using # and 2 paragraphs on what defined this fantasy season.
2. One ## section per storyline (5–7), each a few paragraphs built on the numbers.
3. Close with a ## section on the lesson managers should take into next year's draft.
FANTASY_SEASON_IN_REVIEW.directive:
ARTICLE TYPE SPECIFICATION: Fantasy Season in Review
Granularity: Full season / Story.
Focus: The fantasy season told as a story: the storylines, breakouts and collapses that decided leagues.
Scope: Weeks 1–17 as 5–7 storylines; no awards or lists.
FANTASY_SEASON_IN_REVIEW.example_prompt_hook: Tell the story of this fantasy season: the players who won and lost leagues, and what it means for next year's draft.

FANTASY_AWARDS.name: Fantasy Awards & All-Fantasy Team
FANTASY_AWARDS.focus: The season's fantasy awards and the All-Fantasy Team.
FANTASY_AWARDS.curatorial_autonomy:
CURATORIAL AUTONOMY (FANTASY AWARDS & ALL-FANTASY TEAM):
Hand out: Fantasy MVP, Bust of the Year (highest ADP relative to finish), Waiver Gem (undrafted or drafted in few leagues, finished high), Playoff Hero (Weeks 15–17), and Breakout of the Year. Then name the All-Fantasy Team (QB, 2 RB, 2 WR, TE, FLEX) for the season and a separate one for Weeks 15–17. Use get_fantasy_season_leaders for both ranges and the draft board for ADP and draft %.
FANTASY_AWARDS.structure_directive:
ARTICLE STRUCTURE & FORMATTING DIRECTIVE:
Structure the article as an awards column (at least 1,100 words; longer is fine when the content earns it).

1. Open with a headline using # and a short intro.
2. One ## section per award with the winner in bold, the numbers, and 1–2 runners-up.
3. ## All-Fantasy Team (Season) and ## All-Fantasy Team (Playoffs): position-by-position lists with points.
FANTASY_AWARDS.directive:
ARTICLE TYPE SPECIFICATION: Fantasy Awards & All-Fantasy Team
Granularity: Full season / Awards.
Focus: The season's fantasy awards and the All-Fantasy Team.
Scope: Five awards plus season and playoff All-Fantasy Teams.
FANTASY_AWARDS.example_prompt_hook: Hand out the fantasy season's awards and name the All-Fantasy Teams for the season and the playoffs.

FANTASY_DRAFT_RETRO.name: Draft Retro
FANTASY_DRAFT_RETRO.focus: Looking back at this year's draft: which ADPs were right, which were wrong, and why.
FANTASY_DRAFT_RETRO.curatorial_autonomy:
CURATORIAL AUTONOMY (DRAFT RETRO):
Compare preseason ADP with final positional finish across the board. Cover the best values by round range (rounds 1–3, 4–8, 9–15, undrafted) and the biggest misses, and identify the patterns: which positions or player types the market overrated or underrated. Draft content only: no individual awards (those are in the Awards article).
FANTASY_DRAFT_RETRO.structure_directive:
ARTICLE STRUCTURE & FORMATTING DIRECTIVE:
Structure the article as a draft retrospective (at least 1,100 words; longer is fine when the content earns it).

1. Open with a headline using # and a paragraph on how well this year's draft market did.
2. ## Early Rounds (1–3), ## Middle Rounds (4–8), ## Late Rounds (9–15), ## Undrafted: hits and misses in each, with ADP and finish.
3. ## What the Market Got Wrong: 2–3 patterns to remember next year.
FANTASY_DRAFT_RETRO.directive:
ARTICLE TYPE SPECIFICATION: Draft Retro
Granularity: Full season / Draft Hits & Misses.
Focus: Looking back at this year's draft: which ADPs were right, which were wrong, and why.
Scope: ADP versus final finish, by round range, plus the patterns.
FANTASY_DRAFT_RETRO.example_prompt_hook: Look back at this year's draft: which picks paid off by round, which didn't, and what the market got wrong.

FANTASY_PROJECTION_REPORT_CARD.name: Projection Report Card
FANTASY_PROJECTION_REPORT_CARD.focus: An honest grade of the Mu fantasy projections this season: how close they were, where they missed, and why.
FANTASY_PROJECTION_REPORT_CARD.curatorial_autonomy:
CURATORIAL AUTONOMY (PROJECTION REPORT CARD):
Use get_fantasy_projection_accuracy. Report the overall error and how it compares with simply guessing the average, accuracy by position, and the biggest misses in both directions. Explain the misses in football terms (one huge game, a role change, a surprising touchdown run) using player profiles. Be candid: this is the desk grading its own work.
FANTASY_PROJECTION_REPORT_CARD.structure_directive:
ARTICLE STRUCTURE & FORMATTING DIRECTIVE:
Structure the article as a report card (at least 900 words; longer is fine when the content earns it).

1. Open with a headline using # and a paragraph with the overall grade.
2. ## The Numbers: overall accuracy versus guessing the average, in plain terms.
3. ## By Position: a short paragraph per position with a letter grade.
4. ## The Misses We Learned From: 4–5 biggest misses explained.
5. ## What We'll Change: one closing paragraph.
FANTASY_PROJECTION_REPORT_CARD.directive:
ARTICLE TYPE SPECIFICATION: Projection Report Card
Granularity: Full season / Model Accuracy.
Focus: An honest grade of the Mu fantasy projections this season: how close they were, where they missed, and why.
Scope: The season's projection accuracy, by position, with the biggest misses.
FANTASY_PROJECTION_REPORT_CARD.example_prompt_hook: Grade the Mu fantasy projections honestly: how close they came this season, where they missed, and what that teaches.

FANTASY_DYNASTY_EARLY_LOOK.name: Dynasty Early Look
FANTASY_DYNASTY_EARLY_LOOK.focus: Early rankings for next season and dynasty leagues, weighted toward age and young players' trajectory.
FANTASY_DYNASTY_EARLY_LOOK.curatorial_autonomy:
CURATORIAL AUTONOMY (DYNASTY EARLY LOOK):
Rank the top 25 players for next season with an eye on dynasty value: this season's production and role, weighted by age and experience (rookies and second-year players who produced get a boost; older players with declining usage drop). Use the draft board (age, experience) and season leaders. Include 3–4 young risers outside the top 25.
FANTASY_DYNASTY_EARLY_LOOK.structure_directive:
ARTICLE STRUCTURE & FORMATTING DIRECTIVE:
Structure the article as an early ranking (at least 1,000 words; longer is fine when the content earns it).

1. Open with a headline using # and a paragraph on the league's young core.
2. ## Top 25 for Next Season: numbered, each in bold with team, position, age and a one-sentence case.
3. ## Young Risers: 3–4 players outside the top 25.
4. ## Sell Now in Dynasty: 2–3 older players.
FANTASY_DYNASTY_EARLY_LOOK.directive:
ARTICLE TYPE SPECIFICATION: Dynasty Early Look
Granularity: Next season / Dynasty Rankings.
Focus: Early rankings for next season and dynasty leagues, weighted toward age and young players' trajectory.
Scope: Top 25 for next season, plus young risers and dynasty sells.
FANTASY_DYNASTY_EARLY_LOOK.example_prompt_hook: Rank the top 25 fantasy players for next season, weighted toward age and young players on the rise.
